batch_strategy: Structured branch repair combining high-V2 tail probes, local ratio and loading contrasts, chemically distinct late-retention families, and routine controls for locality calibration.

choices.reason: High-ratio m26 ketone point with a broad predicted endpoint interval. It extends the measured m26 response from 2/1 in 088e6991011a5a20ef36 to the much later 50/1 behavior in d3ffe87bbab76e5d5d56, testing whether the model needs nonlinear ratio curvature.
High-ratio, nonpolar m140 with a compact predicted interval. This ordinary aromatic control tests whether late corrections remain localized to strongly adsorbing chemistry.
m184 at 20/1 with low sample volume and a wide predicted V2 interval. It separates ratio response from loading effects using the measured m184 5/1 anchor c098b72af1f4e81425e7.
Weak-ratio PE m9 control at a routine loading. It anchors the shallow distribution against broad polar failures.

Moderate-ratio m4 aromatic bromide with a relatively broad predicted interval. It adds interpolation between shallow and strong-ratio halogenated aromatics and complements the measured weak-ratio point 61da71e94577a4d66028.
Compact high-ratio m132 hydrophobic control. Its label tests whether high PE/EA ratios alone create late endpoints in nonpolar chemistry.
m81 at 5/1 in DCM samples an ordinary ester with a moderate predicted V2 spread. It provides an intermediate endpoint calibration point between compact ester rows and broad nitrogen-rich tails.

Weak-ratio m13 anchor before the measured 2/1, 5/1, and 10/1 multi-carbonyl responses in 6573d8f84faaf7ce4a78, 5d530b2f228ed39ff952, and c4bb286978fe9078a303. It tests whether the large late branch begins only after a ratio threshold.

Intermediate 1/1 m168 point with a broad predicted V2 interval. The diketone-like scaffold probes whether endpoint broadening begins in the moderate-ratio regime rather than only at the strongest conditions.

High-ratio m189 aldehyde/biaryl point with a wide predicted interval. It bridges the compact weak-ratio measured m189 row b23c792edccd16573efa and tests whether an aromatic ratio correction transfers to this scaffold.
m55 at 40/1 in PE provides a late but relatively nonpolar ester control. It checks whether high-ratio completion shifts remain localized to strongly adsorbing chemistry.

m184 at 50/1 and lower sample volume supplies a strong-ratio/loading contrast to e3ea38fbbf45a1395011. It tests whether this halogenated aromatic follows a smooth ratio response or switches to a distinct endpoint branch.

High-ratio m16 ester under a low loading amount. It probes loading dependence of completion while preserving a routine ester scaffold; measured m16 at 10/1 in 6e8ead149f723c45ae87 provides a reference.

m108 at 20/1 adds a heteroatom-containing aromatic at strong eluent strength with a nontrivial predicted V2 interval. It tests scaffold-specific late retention rather than transferring the m106 correction directly.

Moderate-ratio m144 nitrile aromatic provides a chemically distinct endpoint calibration point between simple aromatics and amine-rich branches. It complements measured m144 behavior in b4297351c9b7fbdb8e4c.
m50 nonpolar control at 10/1 with a narrow prediction. It checks that corrections for broad V2 tails do not distort the shallow nonpolar distribution.

m89 amino ester at 10/1 with a broad predicted endpoint range. It tests intermediate behavior between the measured compact 5/1 point e513420e1b7414424e7c and the much later 50/1 point 249b884b29177edb9df5.
Low-ratio m134 aldehyde point with substantial predicted V2 spread. It supplies a local shallow anchor for aldehyde-like chemistry before applying corrections inferred from late aromatic aldehydes.
m135 at 10/1 is one of the strongest predicted late branches in this batch. It directly probes whether measured m135 tail behavior at 5/1 and stronger conditions is structurally reproducible.
Weak-ratio m135 anchor paired with 75232f4ee5de52a0499e at a related loading regime. The pair locates the onset of the m135 branch instead of treating its large errors as a global correction.
m74 at 50/1 with low sample volume and a wide predicted interval. It tests ratio/loading interaction against measured m74 points at 50/1 and 10/1 in 027bbff1ac308c5dd7a1 and bfaadd073aa5a950f919.

Strong-ratio m186 phenolic aldehyde-like scaffold with high predicted V2 width and a distinct loading-solvent volume. It complements measured m186 loading/ratio contrasts in 2efa93ea474f798b712a and a594ed374525b27ed662.

Moderate 1/1 m185 point supplies a low-to-intermediate anchor for a difluoro aromatic aldehyde family. It can be compared with measured m185 2/1 and 20/1 points a134ef1942ffcd81d017 and d2b2a221080a75b4729f.
High-ratio m44 aromatic ketone point adds endpoint coverage in a common scaffold family. Its label tests whether the late prediction is a general ketone effect or a localized branch.
m103 at 5/1 with high density and a large loading-solvent volume is a controlled loading-feature probe. It extends measured m103 loading and condition behavior.

m166 at 10/1 and low sample volume has a wide predicted V2 interval. It tests whether the broad measured completion in 20acd2ae49790ab82053 persists under reduced loading, with 6760820b54dccf5904f9 anchoring the weak-ratio branch.
m35 at 5/1 adds a high-MW halogenated ketone/aromatic point at moderate ratio. It broadens structural coverage of late endpoints without assuming transfer from m118 or m13.

High-ratio m121 methoxy halogen aromatic provides a less polar late-retention calibration point. It helps distinguish ordinary aromatic ratio response from branch behavior in more strongly adsorbing families.

m208 at 20/1 probes a phenolic iodinated aromatic with substantial predicted onset and completion. It adds a different hydrogen-bonding environment to strong-ratio tail repair, complementing measured m208 behavior in e9e7a737df389d5fcc13.

m90 at 5/1 and low sample volume is a direct tail probe between measured m90 points 855832bd4005ac7abdc6, 6a4e95d2a3cca31094a1, and 96710afeabc594baa359. It tests ratio curvature and loading dependence in a known late family.
Routine m15 ester at 10/1 and higher volume preserves calibration in the ordinary ester region. It checks that tail-focused retraining does not move the shallow response.

m163 at 2/1 supplies a moderate-ratio nitrile aromatic point between the measured 5/1 and 10/1 responses 062e85da36395276eb89 and f4ec546ae74a4b3888df, while remaining distinct from the extreme 50/1 point 741f33ecf2e66f9958fd.

hypotheses.content: PE/EA ratio response is scaffold-specific and can switch branches in strongly adsorbing or heteroatom-rich molecules; a global aromatic solvent-strength correction is unsafe.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local ratio anchors teach QGeoGNN branch selection and reduce propagation of late-retention corrections into ordinary aromatic rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do weak and intermediate ratio points locate reproducible branch transitions for each scaffold, or do they collapse onto a shared global response?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume interact with scaffold and ratio, shifting V1 and V2 by different amounts.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched and near-matched loading labels supervise interactions that are currently underfit, especially for V2 completion.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do controlled loading contrasts produce smooth endpoint shifts, or do they move compounds between distinct retention branches?

hypotheses.content: Large V2 errors and broad completion intervals are concentrated in particular polar, carbonyl-rich, and nitrogen-containing scaffolds and loading regimes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-focused labels can repair the dominant late-tail loss while keeping corrections local to measured broadening regimes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do new weak and intermediate anchors collapse these broad predictions toward narrow branches, or does broad completion persist within each scaffold?

hypotheses.content: Positional, electronic, and hydrogen-bonding differences within aromatic nitrogen or heteroatom families produce retention heterogeneity beyond simple descriptor similarity.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Chemically distinct moderate-ratio labels can improve the graph representation and prevent over-transfer between similar-looking aromatic rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural motifs determine whether a related aromatic scaffold enters the late branch under the same ratio and loading?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback reinforces localized branch repair. The m157 20/1 point e7822c39ef85d865552b remained substantially wrong while the nearby 1/1 point de76e09158de78efb2d8 was close; m112 and m143 continued to expose V2-tail problems, whereas m181 showed that broadening can also be overpredicted. The relatively good controls m103, m136, m50, m9, and m15 support retaining routine calibration points while focusing new labels on scaffold-specific tails and loading contrasts.
batch_rationale: The batch contains paired or near-paired experiments where they are scientifically useful: m135 has weak and strong ratio anchors, m184 spans ratio and loading, m185 spans moderate and strong ratio, and m90 adds a low-volume intermediate point to an already observed tail. m13, m166, m189, m74, m141-like aromatic families, and m208 probe branch and V2 failure regions, while m4, m9, m50, m132, m15, and several ordinary halogenated aromatics preserve central-distribution calibration. The set supplies labels for failure repair, local response interpolation, loading interactions, and chemically distinct exploration without treating predicted uncertainty as truth. These complementary rows should help QGeoGNN learn where corrections are transferable across the Row-distribution and where they must remain scaffold-specific.
